name: retrieval-eval
about: Every expected locator was read off the document, NOT off what retrieval currently returns
(spike §3.1 rule 1). A reviewer checks each grade-2 item against the artefact in knowledge/corpus/
or the paper PDF in pgs_docs/; grading retrieval against its own output is testing_hazards §2.7.
JSON rather than the spike's suggested .yaml because the gate must run on a bare install and
PyYAML is not a dependency of this project (spike §3.1 permits either).
grades:   2 = answers the question (any grade-2 passage counts as a hit)
1 = relevant and supporting, not the answer
0 = plausible but WRONG: its presence measures over-retrieval, never recall
expected: [] = a refusal IS the correct answer. These items are excluded from recall/MRR
because there is nothing to find; they exist so over-retrieval stays measurable
locator:  the chunk's own locator, exactly as `locator_of()` renders it — a SAOSO section_ref
(S20.1.2), an OPP section_ref (§2.1), a content anchor (pgs-sa), or p.<printed page>.
`contains` (case-insensitive, whitespace-collapsed) narrows a locator shared by many
chunks: Appendix 6a has 20 rows on one locator, Appendix 2 has 30, S1 has 8.
A locator that resolves to nothing is a hard error in the runner, never a miss.
asked_by: escalation (a real question a person typed and the bot refused) | probe | uat | curated | design

items.question: What does the standard say about traceability?
items.note: EscalatedQuery NO_CITATIONS. S20.1.2 is the clause that says the word; §6.3 is the group's own traceability requirement for aggregated produce.

items.question: What is the zoning rule for a herd of zebra in Alberta?
items.note: EscalatedQuery INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT. Out of scope twice over: another country's zoning law, and a wild species. A refusal is the correct answer; the word `zoning`/`herd` must not buy a citation.

items.question: Do i need to know where horse manure comes from before I can use it?
items.note: EscalatedQuery NO_CITATIONS/INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT, the most-asked real question in the set. Grade 2 is the Appendix 2 condition (conventional intensive livestock requires prior permission) — the UAT (mvp0 scenario 9) signs this question off on exactly that condition plus the BPP 60-day raw-manure rule.

items.question: Does it say anything about input sourcing?

expected.contains: CRITERIA FOR THE EVALUATION OF INPUTS

items.note: EscalatedQuery NO_CITATIONS. S2.3.3 is the one-step-back tracing rule; Appendix 1 is how SAOSO says an input is evaluated at all.

items.question: can i use horse manure?
items.note: EscalatedQuery NO_CITATIONS (3 rows). The same subject as escalated-horse-manure-origin in five words — kept because a two-word paraphrase is where a lexical-first pipeline is most likely to fail.

items.question: can I use cardboard boxes from my neighbour?
items.note: EscalatedQuery NO_CITATIONS, also UAT mvp0 scenario 10.1. The standard never says 'cardboard', so the governed answer is 4.4.4 + Appendix 2 — the UAT expected outcome is that the answer names the rule and does NOT say cardboard is allowed.

items.question: thanks.  and cardboard boxes from my neighbour?
items.note: EscalatedQuery INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT — a real follow-up fragment. Graded standalone on purpose: the eval runner measures single-turn retrieval, so this row records how much a fragment loses when the parent question is not carried (the context arm's job, D49 stage 1).

items.question: What does the standard say about the minimum rest period for laying hens without artificial light?
items.note: EscalatedQuery — 18 of the 35 stored rows, the single largest source of refusals. Judgement (recorded, not assumed): the standard sets no minimum dark/rest period, so grade 2 is the clause that governs artificial light in livestock housing, which is what a grounded answer must quote instead of inventing a number. Grade 0 is Appendix 6a's `Laying hens 230` — a stocking density is a plausible-sounding answer to a rest-period question, and D73 makes that row easier to retrieve.

items.question: Which fertiliser brand should I buy for tomatoes in George?
items.note: EscalatedQuery INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT, and UAT mvp0 scenario 3. The corpus governs substances, not brands or local shops. `fertiliser` will retrieve Appendix 2 rows — the refusal must come from the audit, not from an empty result set.

items.question: What is the yearly cost to get certified, including the farm visit?
items.note: EscalatedQuery CITATION_AUDIT; also UAT mvp0 scenario 10.5, where the open gap G3 is that the R100 membership fee (§2.1) never arrives. Two grade-2 clauses because 'the yearly cost' is genuinely the sum of the membership fee and the sliding-scale assessment fee.

items.question: can i use purchased silica for supplementation?
items.note: EscalatedQuery CITATION_AUDIT. The Appendix 2 trace-elements row carries the documented-deficiency restriction; Appendix 3 lists a silica product for pest control, which is the wrong frame for a supplement — the only other chunk containing the word.

items.question: what is the definition of genetically modified?  does selective seed saving count as GM?
items.note: EscalatedQuery CITATION_AUDIT. The definitions chunk also defines `Genetic Engineering` and excludes natural hybridisation — that exclusion is the answer to the second half, so both S1 passages are in the set. Resolved by `contains`: eight chunks share locator S1.

items.question: are there any organic ways to manage nutweed/nutsedge? it's a perennial weed
items.note: EscalatedQuery CITATION_AUDIT. `nutsedge` is absent from the corpus (document frequency 0), so this is the unknown-subject path: the answer must come from the weed-management clauses even though the word is not there.

items.question: can I use straw mulch?
items.note: UAT mvp0 scenario 10.2: permitted as a plant material with NO chemical-treatment condition — that condition belongs to the wood row, which is why the wood row is the grade-0 distractor.

items.question: can I use borax for boron supplements?
items.note: UAT mvp0 scenario 10.3: the answer is the trace-elements row plus its documented-deficiency restriction. `borax` itself is never printed — the row lists boric acid and sodium borate.

items.question: if my ducks aren't fed organic food and I make compost from their bedding, will I still pass?

expected.contains: Compost made from ingredients listed in this appendix

items.note: UAT mvp0 scenario 10.6, recorded gap G1: currently refused for an unquotable enumeration. Two hops — the poultry feed rule and the compost-ingredient rule — so a single-clause ranker has no chance; that is the finding, not a grading error.

items.question: how do I sign up?
items.note: UAT mvp0 scenario 10.7. No distinctive noun at all — the hardest shape of question for a lexical-first pipeline.

items.question: if I save seeds from a non-organic seed, are those seeds organic?
items.note: UAT mvp0 scenario 10.7 expects 4.1.2 (one generation under organic management for annuals).

items.question: if a seed is not organic but I grow it organic will the crop be organic?
items.note: UAT mvp0 scenario 10.6, recorded gap G2. The conversion-length clause (4.2.3) is genuinely part of the answer, which is why it is grade 1 rather than absent.

items.question: What does the OPP say about the 'Self-claim organic' labelling category?
items.note: UAT mvp0 scenario 9 step 4. The expected outcome there is a refusal that can still quote the §6.5 prose, so the passage must be retrievable even when the table cell is not.

items.question: how much is the annual membership fee?
items.note: The R100 gap (G3) asked directly. If this question cannot reach §2.1, no amount of prompt work will fix the cost question.

items.question: can we use the SAOSO 'Organic PGS Certified' logo on our product?
items.note: One of the new tables' questions (spike §8.5). The landscape prints no clause numbers, so the locator is a content anchor.

items.question: which certificates and seals can the committee issue to the farmer?
items.note: The seals table's question (spike §8.5) and the claim-discipline boundary: the corpus may describe the seals, the public site may publish only the active ones.

items.question: how many sheep can I run per hectare?
items.note: The row D73 re-embeds verbatim (`Ewes / 13,3`). The question says `sheep`, the table says `Ewes`: the shared-word problem in one line. S2.2.4 is the requirement the number serves.

items.question: how many laying hens per hectare?
items.note: Measured 2026-10-29 in TABLES_AS_DATA_PRD §7 Q5: this exact question returns NO hits at all, because `websearch_to_tsquery` ANDs its terms. It is the baseline Q1 is measured against.

items.question: how many cows per hectare?
items.note: Three Appendix 6a rows contain `cows` (Dairy cows, Cull dairy cows, Other cows). Grade 2 resolves on `dairy cows`; the ambiguity is the finding — row-level retrieval is what D73 is being priced for.

items.question: how long is the conversion period for plant production?
items.note: A question the standard answers with a number (12 months), and one a member asks in their first year.

items.question: how far must my beehives be from conventional fields?
items.note: Two distances in adjacent clauses (5 km from contamination risk, 3 km organic foraging) — a rank-2 answer here is a wrong number, not a near miss, which is why MRR is reported alongside recall.

items.question: how long can the trip to the slaughterhouse be?
items.note: Eight hours, with the derogation attached. `slaughterhouse` occurs in this clause and in the transport section only.

items.question: can my children help on the farm?
items.note: S23.9 sets the child-labour rule and the regional exception for family labour; the section opener (S23) carries the general principle.

items.question: can I buy in produce from a conventional neighbour and sell it as PGS certified?
items.note: The aggregation boundary in the OPP's own words: permitted with minimum safeguards, never as 'certified organic'.

items.question: can the PGS visit my farm without warning?
items.note: §4.1 gives 5 days' notice, §4.4 reserves the right to arrive unannounced. Both are needed for an honest answer.

items.question: can I label my product as 'in conversion'?
items.note: Two clauses govern it (the 12-month minimum and the distinguishable label) and they live in different sections.

items.question: at what temperature can I heat honey?
items.note: 45 °C. Short numeric answer, so the top rank is the whole result.

items.question: do I need a permit to sell raw milk?
items.note: The spike's own example of an unanswerable question (§3.1). `permit` and `raw milk` do not occur in the corpus, but `permitted` does — so retrieval returns a full set and only the audit can refuse. This is the item that proves a non-empty result set is not evidence of coverage.
